Saanvi identified “ten and one” as eleven with prompting.
Saanvi said fourteen and four loose ones, but confused the ten bundle with the digit 1.
The bundle-versus-loose-ones mix-up was not corrected by the last response; teach-back was not passed.

end.parentNote: Saanvi practised making numbers 11–20 with one group of ten and extra ones. They could say fourteen and notice four loose ones, but mixed up the group of ten with the digit 1; this was still unresolved when they stopped. At home, make a bundle of 10 straws and add loose straws—for example, one bundle plus 4 loose straws makes 14—then ask Saanvi to say both parts.
